order: agent-multi@c900656a — R1-R5, real cancellation and flatten recovery
note: PRE reproduced and frozen BEFORE any edit. All four findings confirmed.

R1_reference_coercion.verdict: register_order_role accepted float and applied int(), so 1.5 became identity 1 and 2.9 became 2 — real identities belonging to other live orders. A silent collision could attach the wrong role to a live order.

R2_no_real_cancellation.verdict: the committed test injected ref 4242, which never existed in backtrader's book, so the expected outcome was 'not_open'. It proved the request reached the strategy and nothing more: no real order was ever cancelled, and the race against a fill at the next bar's open was untested. The principal economic risk of C2 was unproven.

R3_reset_erases_the_obligation.verdict: an in-flight close obligation VANISHED on reset and the next episode started clean by forgetting it. The committed test asserted this as correct behaviour, so it encoded the defect.

R4_freshness_is_a_constant.verdict: the age was asserted, not derived from any observation instant, and the check was not labelled as simulator-local evidence.

refused.1.5: order ref must be a non-boolean int identity, got float 1.5 — no coercion
refused.2.9: order ref must be a non-boolean int identity, got float 2.9 — no coercion
refused.3.0: refused — a float is not an identity even when integral

R2_real_cancellation_end_to_end.method: a genuine resting Limit BUY entry is submitted THROUGH THE EXECUTING PATH by a strategy plugin, registered as 'entry' like any other order, and sized to fit the cash the open position leaves free so the broker ACCEPTS it. The synthetic not_open fixture is retained separately as an incident test, never as evidence of an executed cancellation.
R2_real_cancellation_end_to_end.5_both_brackets_alive_through_wind_down: refs 4 and 5, protective_stop and protective_take_profit, present at every WIND_DOWN bar; retired by the CLOSE at bar 6

R3_durable_obligation_and_fail_closed_re.mechanism: app/flatten_custody.py::FlattenObligationStore writes the obligation durably at the moment it is requested, reusing the migration custody's audited no-overwrite protocol: O_EXCL creation, 0600, fsync of file and parent, symlink refusal, and an exclusive transition lock with expected-state identity. reset() no longer clears the attempt; it RE-READS custody.

discharge.rule: recovery lifts ONLY on fresh evidence of zero positions AND zero orders, and the discharge is written to durable custody, not only to memory.

R3_durable_obligation_and_fail_closed_re.self_reported_defect_1: my first obligation id was flatten-ep{bridge.episode_seq}-bar{n}. bridge.episode_seq restarts at 1 for every new bridge, so the second episode collided and the store correctly refused. The identity now carries a per-process, per-env run token.
R3_durable_obligation_and_fail_closed_re.self_reported_defect_2: my first store passed the record's OWN current state as the expected state to the terminal transition, so the expected-state check matched itself and a confirmed obligation could be overwritten by a later fail(). A terminal obligation is now explicitly immutable and only an open state may be closed.
R3_durable_obligation_and_fail_closed_re.unreadable_records: a record that cannot be parsed counts as OUTSTANDING: an unreadable file is not evidence that the obligation was discharged.

R4_reconciliation_provenance.monotonic_clock: a bar index that goes backwards is a typed refusal
R4_reconciliation_provenance.max_age_configurable: session_max_evidence_age_seconds, default 120.0, no longer hardcoded at the call site
R4_reconciliation_provenance.wp3_boundary: venue_direct is False. WP3 must replace this with typed DIRECT venue evidence; any consumer requiring venue authority must refuse on this provenance, and the zero-age literal may not be inherited.

not_done: No deployment. The live MT5 position was not touched. No training launched. No live parity claimed. WP3 remains blocked pending independent acceptance of R1-R4; WP4 remains behind WP3 live parity.
